asset.content:
Subject: Map a client project on paper
Preview text: Organise 16 undated weeks with goal breakdowns and three planning views.

Plan a client project across 16 weeks

Hello,

Map a substantial client project across 16 weeks on paper.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner gives freelance work a bounded structure: 16 weeks of undated planning pages, supported by goal breakdowns.

Start with the project goal, then organise the work through monthly, weekly and daily planning pages. Each view offers a different planning cadence while keeping the project on paper.

Because the pages are undated, you choose where the 16-week plan begins.

Open the product page’s Look inside view to review the goal-planning space and monthly, weekly and daily layouts, then decide whether the structure suits your client-project workflow.

Look inside the planner → https://www.papier.com/your-plans-on-paper-57101

- Papier

asset_metadata.body:
Map a substantial client project across 16 weeks on paper.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner gives freelance work a bounded structure: 16 weeks of undated planning pages, supported by goal breakdowns.

Start with the project goal, then organise the work through monthly, weekly and daily planning pages. Each view offers a different planning cadence while keeping the project on paper.

asset_metadata.single_idea: A focused client project can be mapped across 16 undated weeks using documented goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.

selected_brief.selection_reason: The bounded 16-week format directly matches the selected audience's focused push, while goal breakdowns and multiple planning cadences give a freelancer a concrete way to organise a client project on paper.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a freelancer with a substantial client project, the planner can provide one paper structure for breaking down the goal and organising work across monthly, weekly and daily views during a focused 16-week period.
value_case.mechanism: The productivity planner uses 16 weeks of undated pages with goal breakdowns, while the Your Plans on Paper planner includes monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
decision_conditions: The documented format is undated and spans 16 weeks.
The evidence does not establish a continuous rolling-date view or links between notes and dates.

selected_brief.target_audience: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
selected_brief.job: Help the reader judge whether this planner's paper structure fits the way they want to organise a focused client project.
selected_brief.single_idea: A focused client project can be mapped across 16 undated weeks using documented goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
selected_brief.mechanism: Present the planner as a bounded paper framework: set out the project across 16 undated weeks, break down the goal, and use monthly, weekly and daily pages to organise the work at different levels.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a distinct consideration argument for a freelancer who values reviewing how they work during a project, rather than primarily needing multiple planning cadences.

value_case.reader_benefit: During a focused client project, the reader can use documented accountability tools and reflections to record progress and consider their working patterns.
value_case.mechanism: The productivity planner combines accountability tracking tools and progress reflections with articles intended to help users understand their working patterns.
decision_conditions: The individual accountability tools and the number or subjects of the articles are not specified.
No improvement in productivity or project results is established.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: The planner supports an ongoing review habit through accountability tracking tools, progress reflections and articles about working patterns.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Accountability tracking tools provide a place to record execution, reflections support progress review, and accompanying articles are intended to help the reader understand working patterns.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: the reader may see the planner mainly as a place to schedule work. After: they understand that it also contains documented tools for reviewing progress and working patterns during a project.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner improves productivity, accountability, project delivery or working patterns.
Do not describe the unnamed productivity pillars or unspecified accountability tools in greater detail.
Do not imply testimonials, widespread adoption or measured results.
Do not invent prior visits, conversations, discounts, urgency or purchase history.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether progress reflection and accountability support are useful enough for the reader's client-project workflow.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The page describes the planner's articles, accountability tracking tools and reflections so the reader can assess that approach.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page description does not establish measured outcomes or specify every accountability tool.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the planner as a way to review a focused project's progress, using concrete language about reflection and accountability without promising improved performance.

selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: the reader knows Papier but may not know how this planner is structured for a bounded project. After: they understand the documented 16-week planning mechanism and can inspect whether its layouts suit their work.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner provides a continuous current-day-centred or rolling calendar view.
Do not claim that notes can be linked to dates, digital calendars, Obsidian or other software.
Do not guarantee goal achievement, productivity gains, time savings, focus or successful project delivery.
Do not present the fit as established for all professionals; keep the reader within freelancers delivering a client project.
Do not invent the reader's current tools, missed deadlines, strict task-management frustrations or prior Papier activity.
Do not mention customer proof, comparative superiority, pricing, discounts, scarcity or urgency.
Do not invent prior visits, conversations or purchase intent.
The planner documents monthly, weekly and daily planning pages, but not a rolling current-day-centered calendar or links between notes and dates.
selected_brief.tone: Professional, polished and quietly confident; concise, credible and lightly artful without slang or hype.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Decide whether the planner's goal-planning space and monthly, weekly and daily pages suit the reader's client-project workflow.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The product page lets the reader look inside and review the documented goal-planning space and monthly, weekly and daily planning structure.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: Inspecting the layouts does not establish a continuous rolling-date view, linked-note functionality or any customer outcome.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete 16-week paper-planning structure for a focused project; signal useful specificity to a product-aware reader without explaining the category or promising results.

directions: Write exactly one consideration email in English.
Address a prospect who already knows Papier but has not bought.
Explain one useful supported aspect of the offering and provide a documented next step.
Use a professional and polished tone: confident and credible, with no slang or hype.
use: Monthly, weekly and daily planning pages
context_only: The single-source audience problem concerning continuous calendars and linked daily notes

email.headline: Plan a client project across 16 weeks
email.body:
Sixteen weeks is long enough for a substantial client project and short enough to keep in view. On paper, the whole run can sit in one place.

Papier's Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner gives that run a bounded structure: 16 weeks of undated pages, supported by goal breakdowns. Because nothing is pre-dated, you decide where week one falls.

From there, monthly, weekly and daily planning pages organise the work at three cadences. The product page's Look inside view shows the goal-planning space and those layouts, so you can judge whether they suit your client-project workflow.
